assembly_instructions: Lay out the port and starboard carbon-fiber skid tubes parallel to the X axis with their lower faces on y = 0, then bolt the front and rear skid cross-tubes between them to form the ground-contact sled frame.
Install the four vertical cabin risers on the skid tubes and add the diagonal skid braces so the risers triangulate back into the sled rather than carrying cabin loads as isolated posts.
Bolt the carbon-fiber cabin floor pan to the four risers; this floor pan is the structural root for passengers, batteries, cabin shell, and boom roots.
Install the battery service rails, exposed battery pack, avionics tray, avionics bay, touchscreen console, cooling ducts, and wiring harnesses while the port side remains open for inspection.

Bond the rear bulkhead, starboard side shell, roof panel, windshield frame, roof hoops, side sills, hinge spars, nose fairing panels, tail fairing panels, and glazing to the cabin floor, leaving the port wall removed as a permanent cutaway.
Attach the four dark-anodized V-support root blocks and the four visible motor-controller boxes to the underside corners of the cabin floor.
Fasten the eight carbon-fiber rotor arms outward from the root blocks in the EH216-S 22.5 degree spaced planform and route each harness channel through its arm.
Install the lower and upper motor cans at each arm tip on the common coaxial axis, wiring each motor back through its root motor controller to the exposed battery pack.

Fit each propeller hub and crossed carbon-fiber blade pair to the 16 motors, checking that representative pitch strips identify fixed-pitch blade twist and that upper and lower rotor planes remain separated.
Mount the gull-wing door panels, side windows, command-link antenna, anti-collision strobe, and port/starboard navigation lights.

Perform final build checks: skids sit on the ground line, no rotor intersects the cabin shell, every motor has its own propeller and power path, and the cutaway exposes seats, battery, avionics, cooling, and command electronics without hidden opaque blocks.

info.summary: Two-seat autonomous multirotor eVTOL air taxi from EHang — the world's first pilotless passenger-carrying aircraft to be granted a Type Certificate (CAAC, October 2023), followed by Production and Standard Airworthiness Certificates.
info.description: The EH216-S is a passenger-carrying autonomous aerial vehicle (AAV) developed by Guangzhou EHang Intelligent Technology. It is a true "drone-style" flying car: a car-like composite cabin seats two passengers under a panoramic windshield, with gull-wing doors and sled-style landing gear. Beneath the cabin floor, four V-shaped supports radiate outward from the cabin's lower-side corners in an X pattern; each V forks into two horizontal arms, and each of the eight arm tips mounts a coaxial pair of brushless motors driving fixed-pitch composite propellers — sixteen rotors in all, with the upper rotor disk sitting just below the cabin floor and the lower disk between the cabin floor and the skids, so the rotor structure occupies the lower third of the airframe envelope. There is no onboard pilot and no flight stick: passengers select a destination on a touchscreen and the aircraft executes a pre-cleared route under supervision from a ground command-and-control center. The Civil Aviation Administration of China (CAAC) accepted the type-certification application in January 2021 and issued the Type Certificate on 13 October 2023 — the world's first TC for a pilotless passenger-carrying eVTOL. A Production Certificate and a Standard Airworthiness Certificate followed in 2024, clearing the EH216-S for serial manufacture and commercial operation.

facts.label: Configuration

facts.label: Length x Width x Height
facts.value: 5.61 m x 5.73 m x 1.93 m full-scale airframe

facts.label: Scene scale
facts.value: Model uses full metres with rotor-tip envelope kept below 6 m span

facts.value: Pilotless passenger touchscreen plus ground command-and-control supervision

parts.name: Landing Skid Tube (Port)
parts.role: Port sled tube is the left ground-contact runner and spreads landing loads along the cabin length.

parts.name: Landing Skid Tube (Starboard)
parts.role: Starboard sled tube is the right ground-contact runner and mirrors the port landing-load path.

parts.name: Forward Skid Cross-Tube
parts.role: Forward cross-tube fixes skid spacing and carries nose-down landing side loads between the runners.

parts.name: Aft Skid Cross-Tube
parts.role: Aft cross-tube closes the sled frame and resists yaw loads during touchdown.

parts.name: Cabin Riser (Fwd-Port)
parts.role: Forward-port vertical post transfers cabin floor load into the port skid tube.

parts.name: Cabin Riser (Aft-Port)
parts.role: Aft-port vertical post supports the rear cabin floor corner above the port skid.

parts.name: Cabin Riser (Fwd-Starboard)
parts.role: Forward-starboard vertical post transfers cabin floor load into the starboard skid tube.

parts.name: Cabin Riser (Aft-Starboard)
parts.role: Aft-starboard vertical post supports the rear cabin floor corner above the starboard skid.

parts.name: Skid Diagonal Brace (Fwd-Port)
parts.role: Diagonal brace triangulates the forward-port riser into the sled frame to prevent fore-aft rocking.

parts.name: Skid Diagonal Brace (Aft-Port)
parts.role: Diagonal brace triangulates the aft-port riser and keeps the port skid from splaying outward.

parts.name: Skid Diagonal Brace (Fwd-Starboard)
parts.role: Diagonal brace triangulates the forward-starboard riser into the sled frame.

parts.name: Skid Diagonal Brace (Aft-Starboard)
parts.role: Diagonal brace triangulates the aft-starboard riser and stabilizes the landing sled.

parts.name: Cabin Floor Pan
parts.role: Thin carbon-fiber floor pan is the main structural datum for passengers, batteries, cabin shell, and boom roots.

parts.name: Battery Service Rail (Port)
parts.role: Port service rail supports the removable battery pack and shows how the pack slides into the floor bay.

parts.name: Battery Service Rail (Starboard)
parts.role: Starboard service rail mirrors the port rail and fixes the battery pack laterally in the exposed bay.

parts.name: Avionics Equipment Tray
parts.role: Thin tray bolts to the floor and gives the exposed flight-control bay a buildable mounting shelf.

parts.name: Cutaway Cabin Roof Panel
parts.role: Composite roof panel is shifted toward starboard so the ISO-facing port side remains open and interior systems stay visible.

parts.name: Starboard Cabin Side Shell
parts.role: Opaque starboard shell panel shows the cabin outer skin while the opposite port side is removed for the cutaway.

parts.name: Rear Cabin Bulkhead
parts.role: Rear composite bulkhead closes the passenger cell and gives the avionics bay a visible mounting face.

parts.name: Forward Windshield Frame
parts.role: Forward frame carries the panoramic windshield and ties the nose fairing into the floor pan.

parts.name: Panoramic Windshield
parts.role: Large forward glazing identifies the passenger pod and remains transparent-looking against the white composite frame.

parts.name: Rounded Nose Fairing
parts.role: Rounded forward fairing houses forward sensors and gives the EH216-S its car-like nose silhouette.

parts.name: Tapered Nose Upper Fairing
parts.role: Tapered upper fairing blends the windshield frame into the rounded nose instead of leaving a box-to-sphere joint.

parts.name: Tapered Nose Lower Fairing
parts.role: Lower tapered fairing forms the chin of the passenger pod and carries the forward sensor window.

parts.name: Forward Sensor Window
parts.role: Dark sensor window marks the forward radar and vision payload inside the nose fairing.

parts.name: Rounded Tail Fairing
parts.role: Rounded aft fairing covers the rear service bay and completes the short passenger-pod silhouette.

parts.name: Tapered Tail Upper Fairing
parts.role: Upper tail fairing tapers the roof panel into the aft cap and removes the abrupt rear box silhouette.

parts.name: Tapered Tail Lower Fairing
parts.role: Lower tail fairing closes the underside of the aft service bay while leaving the cutaway interior visible from port.

parts.name: Forward Roof Arch Hoop
parts.role: Forward roof hoop is a visible cutaway frame member spanning across the passenger cell.

parts.name: Rear Roof Arch Hoop
parts.role: Rear roof hoop frames the cutaway opening and ties the roof panel to the rear bulkhead.

parts.name: Open Port Side Sill
parts.role: Port sill marks the removed cabin wall edge so seats, console, battery, avionics, and wiring remain visible from ISO.

parts.name: Starboard Side Sill
parts.role: Starboard sill supports the intact side shell and door panel.

parts.name: Gull-Wing Door Panel (Port, Raised Cutaway)
parts.role: Raised port gull-wing door is shown open so it identifies the door mechanism without covering the cabin interior.

parts.name: Gull-Wing Door Panel (Starboard)
parts.role: Closed starboard gull-wing door shows the outer passenger access panel on the intact side.

parts.name: Port Door Hinge Spar
parts.role: Port hinge spar explains how the raised gull-wing door attaches to the roof edge.

parts.name: Starboard Door Hinge Spar
parts.role: Starboard hinge spar locates the closed gull-wing door along the roof edge.

parts.name: Port Door Window
parts.role: Small port glazing remains attached to the raised door and confirms this is the passenger access side.

parts.name: Starboard Side Window
parts.role: Tinted starboard window sits in the intact gull-wing door and balances the exposed port cutaway.

parts.name: Passenger Seat (Port)
parts.role: Port passenger seat is visible through the removed side wall and carries one half of the 220 kg rated payload.

parts.name: Passenger Seat Back (Port)
parts.role: Port seat back shows the reclining passenger orientation inside the autonomous cabin.

parts.name: Passenger Seat (Starboard)
parts.role: Starboard passenger seat forms the second side-by-side occupant position in the two-seat cabin.

parts.name: Passenger Seat Back (Starboard)
parts.role: Starboard seat back makes the second passenger station legible behind the windshield.

parts.name: Passenger Touchscreen Console
parts.role: Central touchscreen is the passenger interface for destination selection in place of pilot controls.

parts.name: Exposed Battery Pack
parts.role: Visible lithium-polymer battery pack sits below the seats and feeds independent channels to all 16 motor controllers.

parts.name: Exposed Avionics and Flight-Control Bay
parts.role: Exposed avionics bay contains redundant flight controllers, IMUs, GNSS receivers, and command-link electronics.

parts.name: Console Data Harness
parts.role: Low-voltage harness links the passenger touchscreen to the exposed flight-control bay.

parts.name: Port Power Harness
parts.role: Port high-current harness routes battery output toward the two port-side V-root motor controllers.

parts.name: Starboard Power Harness
parts.role: Starboard high-current harness routes battery output toward the two right-side V-root motor controllers.

parts.name: Port Cabin Cooling Duct
parts.role: Port duct makes avionics cooling visible in the open cutaway instead of hiding it inside the rear bulkhead.

parts.name: Starboard Cabin Cooling Duct
parts.role: Starboard duct mirrors the port cooling path for the enclosed side of the electronics bay.

parts.name: V-Support Root (Forward-Port)
parts.role: Forward-port machined root block bolts two rotor arms into the cabin floor corner.

parts.name: V-Support Root (Aft-Port)
parts.role: Aft-port machined root block anchors the rear-left V-support to the floor pan.

parts.name: V-Support Root (Aft-Starboard)
parts.role: Aft-starboard machined root block anchors the rear-right V-support to the floor pan.

parts.name: V-Support Root (Forward-Starboard)
parts.role: Forward-starboard machined root block bolts the right-front V-support into the floor pan.

parts.name: Forward-Port Motor Controller Box
parts.role: Controller box converts battery power into three-phase drive for the two forward-port coaxial motor pairs.

parts.name: Aft-Port Motor Controller Box
parts.role: Controller box powers the two aft-port coaxial motor pairs through the port arm wiring.

parts.name: Aft-Starboard Motor Controller Box
parts.role: Controller box powers the two aft-starboard coaxial motor pairs through the right rear V-support.

parts.name: Forward-Starboard Motor Controller Box
parts.role: Controller box powers the forward-starboard coaxial motor pairs and completes the visible redundant power layout.

parts.role: Forward fork of the forward-port V-support carries the 22.5 degree coaxial motor pair.

parts.name: V-Arm Q1B to 67.5 Degree Rotor
parts.role: Outboard fork of the forward-port V-support carries the 67.5 degree coaxial motor pair.

parts.name: V-Arm Q2A to 112.5 Degree Rotor
parts.role: Outboard fork of the aft-port V-support carries the 112.5 degree coaxial motor pair.

parts.name: V-Arm Q2B to 157.5 Degree Rotor
parts.role: Aft fork of the aft-port V-support carries the 157.5 degree coaxial motor pair.

parts.role: Aft fork of the aft-starboard V-support carries the 202.5 degree coaxial motor pair.

parts.name: V-Arm Q3B to 247.5 Degree Rotor
parts.role: Outboard fork of the aft-starboard V-support carries the 247.5 degree coaxial motor pair.

parts.name: V-Arm Q4A to 292.5 Degree Rotor
parts.role: Outboard fork of the forward-starboard V-support carries the 292.5 degree coaxial motor pair.

parts.name: V-Arm Q4B to 337.5 Degree Rotor
